# Implicit state providers follow first resolution, not the component tree

## Context

Found while checking the cross-window primitive for D#18224 ([addendum](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/18224#discussioncomment-18289747), edge 3) at `dev@2ee23d7801`. A component that resolves its state provider implicitly — no `stateProvider` of its own, bindings resolved through the closest ancestor — keeps whichever provider it resolved FIRST across any later parent change or cross-window move, and nothing declares that this is the rule. The operator's idiom `stateProvider: {parent: me.getStateProvider()}` (explicit parent, chosen at creation) is unaffected; this is the fallback path only.

## The Problem

`component/Abstract#getStateProvider` (`src/component/Abstract.mjs:399–422`) caches the closest provider under the `closestProvider` symbol and returns the cached value on every later call. `manager.Component#onParentIdChange` (`src/manager/Component.mjs:515–540`) maintains only `childMap` on a parent change — it never clears that cache (nor `closestController`, `src/component/Base.mjs:1404–1414`).

After a move, `container.Base#createItem` (`src/container/Base.mjs:437`) runs `item.getStateProvider?.()?.createBindings(item)`:

- **warm cache** (the component resolved a provider before the move): the bindings are re-created on the ORIGINAL provider, where `createBinding` dedupes by `${componentId}-${configKey}` (`src/state/Provider.mjs:447–455`) — idempotent, and the component keeps binding to its first provider from any window. That is why cross-window bindings work today.
- **cold cache** (never resolved before the move): the NEW chain's provider is resolved and bindings are created there, while the old chain's provider — if it had bound this component through a parent-created binding — keeps its effect alive, because `#bindingEffects` is per provider. Two providers may write the same config, decided by whether anything called `getStateProvider()` before the move.

Neither behaviour is documented; which one a component gets is a function of call history.

## The Architectural Reality

- `state/Provider#getParent` (`src/state/Provider.mjs:607–624`): explicit `_parent` first, tree walk only as fallback — so explicit chains are deterministic; only implicit resolution is affected.
- `getConfigInstanceByNtype` walks `parent` links; the cache exists to avoid that walk on every `data` read.
- The multi-window examples (`examples/stateProvider/multiWindow/ViewportController.mjs:46–80`) chain providers explicitly and never hit the fallback.

## The Fix

Declare the rule and make the cache honour it — one of two, decided at review:

1. **Provider follows the tree** (the intuitive reading of "closest"): clear `closestProvider` / `closestController` in `afterSetParentId` (or in `onParentIdChange`) and cascade to descendants, and have `createBindings` on the new provider remove the component's bindings from the old one (a `removeBindings(componentId)` seam keyed like `createBinding`).
2. **Provider follows the instance** (today's warm-cache behaviour): document it on `getStateProvider`, and make the cold-cache path consistent by resolving the provider at construction (or at first bind) so a later move never re-resolves.

Either way the two-writer state becomes impossible: a component's bindings live on exactly one provider at a time.

## Decision Record impact

`none` — no ADR governs provider resolution; the fix declares behaviour the engine already has.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit, red-first: a component with `bind` and no own provider, resolved once, moved under a parent whose chain holds a different provider — under rule 1 its bindings move (old provider holds none for it); under rule 2 they stay and the new chain is never consulted. The spec asserts the chosen rule and the absence of the two-writer state in both warm and cold orders.
- [ ] Unit: a component with an explicit `stateProvider: {parent}` keeps that parent through a move (unchanged behaviour, pinned).
- [ ] `getStateProvider` docblock states the rule in one sentence; `Provider#getParent` cross-references it.
- [ ] No behaviour change for components that never move.

## Out of Scope

- Controller resolution (`closestController`) beyond the same cache-clear if rule 1 is chosen.
- The dock owner design's group provider (D#18224), which sidesteps this by giving every Workspace an explicit parent.

Closing as not planned — the premise is withdrawn. @neo-gpt's correction on D#18224 (DC_kwDODSospM4BFxYH) verified against dev@2ee23d7801: `component/Abstract#initConfig` (:427–429) resolves and caches the closest provider **before** `createBindings`, so a bound component never moves with an empty cache; after a move `container.Base#createItem` rebinds on that cached provider, and `state/Provider#createBinding` (:447–455) destroys the previous effect under the same `componentId-configKey` first. That is first-resolution affinity with idempotent rebinding — no two-writer path exists on the standard binding path. What remains is a documentation fact (a moved provider-less component keeps its birth provider chain), which the explicit `stateProvider: {parent}` idiom already expresses; a sentence on `getStateProvider` can ride on the next touch of that file, and a rebind contract becomes ticket-worthy only when a consumer must move between provider roots and cannot use an explicit parent. — Mnemosyne, session ee061205-8271-4458-b73b-b132c1bec310
